data.summary: The 12‑week plan spreads the 2‑hour weekly study load across all AP Calculus AB units, beginning with the weak units (7 and 8) and revisiting them before the exam. Early weeks introduce differential equations and integration applications, then move through limits, differentiation, and integration fundamentals. The final two weeks are dedicated to mixed review and timed practice, ensuring the student consolidates knowledge and hones test‑taking speed.

weeks.focus: Introduce differential equations and practice basic modeling.
tasks: Read the unit overview for Unit 7 and watch a short video on modeling with differential equations.
Do 5 practice problems on setting up differential equations from word problems.
Verify solutions for each problem using the provided answer key.

weeks.focus: Continue differential equations and begin slope‑field interpretation.
tasks: Sketch slope fields for 3 given differential equations.
Answer 5 conceptual questions interpreting behavior from slope fields.
Complete a short quiz checking ability to verify solutions (7.2).

weeks.focus: Introduce applications of integration and average value.
tasks: Read the section on average value of a function (8.1).
Solve 4 problems finding average values on given intervals.
Work through 3 problems connecting position, velocity, and acceleration using integrals (8.2).

weeks.focus: Further integration applications and area between curves.
tasks: Do 5 problems applying accumulation functions in real‑world contexts (8.3).
Calculate areas between curves for 4 pairs of functions (8.4).
Review notes from weeks 1‑3 and create a one‑page summary of key formulas.
Watch a tutorial on limit notation and algebraic properties.
Complete 8 limit‑evaluation problems covering each sub‑topic.
Estimate limits from graphs and tables for 4 additional examples.

weeks.focus: Differentiation basics – rates of change and power rule.
tasks: Derive the derivative definition for 2 functions and compute instantaneous rates (2.1‑2.2).
Estimate derivatives at given points (2.3) for 5 functions.
Practice applying the power rule on 10 polynomial functions (2.5).
Explain why differentiability implies continuity in a short paragraph (2.4).
Solve 4 chain‑rule problems involving trigonometric and exponential functions (3.1).
Complete 3 implicit differentiation exercises (3.2).
Differentiate inverse functions for 2 cases (3.3).
Practice differentiating inverse trig functions (3.4) with 3 problems.

weeks.focus: Contextual applications of differentiation – related rates and motion.
tasks: Interpret derivative meaning in 3 real‑world scenarios (4.1).
Work through 4 straight‑line motion problems linking position, velocity, acceleration (4.2).
Solve 3 non‑motion rate‑of‑change problems (4.3).
Complete 2 related‑rates problems (4.4).

weeks.focus: Analytical applications – extrema and first‑derivative test.
tasks: Apply the Mean Value Theorem to 3 functions (5.1).
Identify critical points and classify extrema for 5 functions (5.2‑5.4).
Determine intervals of increase/decrease for 4 functions (5.3).

weeks.focus: Integration fundamentals – Riemann sums and FTC.
tasks: Explore accumulation of change with 2 short simulations (6.1).
Compute areas using left, right, and midpoint Riemann sums for 4 functions (6.2).
Write definite integrals using summation notation for 3 examples (6.3).
Apply the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus to evaluate 5 integrals (6.4).

weeks.focus: Mixed review – revisit weak units and key concepts.
tasks: Do a set of 6 mixed problems: 2 differential‑equation modeling, 2 slope‑field interpretation, 1 average‑value integration, 1 area‑between‑curves.
Review notes and create a one‑page cheat sheet of formulas for Units 7 and 8.
Take a 15‑minute timed quiz covering the listed topics.

weeks.focus: Full‑length timed practice and final review.
tasks: Complete a 30‑question timed practice set covering all listed topics.
Mark answers against the scoring guide and note any remaining weak areas.
Review incorrect problems and rewrite solutions correctly.

data.final_week_advice: On the last week, focus on pacing and accuracy. Simulate exam conditions, use the cheat sheet only for quick reference, and spend any remaining time reviewing the specific problems you missed. Ensure you are comfortable with calculator use and the free‑response format before the exam day.
